easy.def: A notice or short film that tries to get you to buy something.
examples: I saw an ad on TV.
The ad is for cereal.
The ad was funny.

more.def: A short word for advertisement, a message that tries to sell something.
examples: I saw an ad for a new toy.
The ad on the radio was funny.
They put an ad in the paper for the sale.

easy.def: To change to fit a new place or a new way of doing things.
examples: Animals adapt to the cold.
I adapted to my new school.
We adapt to the heat.

more.def: To change yourself or something else so that it works well in a new place or situation.
examples: Polar bears have adapted to life in the freezing Arctic.
It took me a week to adapt to my new school.
She adapted the story into a short play for the class.

related.def: Able to change to fit new things.
A change made to fit something new.
A thing that lets two different parts fit together.

easy.def: To put one thing with another.
examples: Add milk to the cereal.
She added sugar.
He adds a block.

more.def: To put one thing together with another.
examples: Add two cups of flour to the bowl.
She added a picture to her poster.
Please add your name to the list.

easy.def: To find the total of numbers.
examples: Add two and three.
We add numbers in math.
She adds the prices.

more.def: To find the total of two or more numbers.
examples: If you add four and five, you get nine.
We learned to add in first grade.
She added up the prices to see the cost.

easy.def: A small snake with marks down its back.
examples: An adder lay in the sun.
The adder is a snake.
We saw an adder.

more.def: A small snake with a dark zigzag pattern along its back, found in parts of Europe and Asia.
examples: The adder slid quietly through the heather.
An adder usually hides when people come near.
The adder warmed itself on a flat rock.

easy.def: Putting numbers together.
examples: We learned addition.
Addition is adding.
Two plus two is addition.

more.def: The math process of finding the total of two or more numbers.
examples: We learned addition in first grade.
Addition is the opposite of subtraction.
I am good at addition.

easy.def: Something that is added.
examples: The baby is a new addition to the family.
A new room is an addition.
The pool is an addition.

more.def: Something that is added to what is already there.
examples: The baby is a new addition to our family.
A new room was an addition to the house.
The puppy is a happy addition to our home.

easy.def: Extra.
examples: I need additional paper.
An additional chair.
There is an additional fee.

more.def: More than what was there before, extra.
examples: I need an additional sheet of paper.
We set out an additional chair for the guest.
There is an additional charge for the ride.

easy.def: The name of the street where you live.
examples: What is your address?
I know my address.
Write your address on the letter.

more.def: The number, street and town that tell where a person lives or where a business is.
examples: Write your address on the envelope.
Our address is 12 Oak Street.
The library's address is on the sign.

easy.def: To give a speech to people.
examples: The mayor will address the crowd.
The principal addressed the school.
She addresses the class.

more.def: To speak formally to a group.
examples: The principal addressed the students at assembly.
The mayor addressed the crowd in the park.
She addressed the audience from the stage.

easy.def: Enough, but not great.
examples: We have adequate food.
The room is adequate.
Her work was adequate.

more.def: Good enough or big enough for what is needed, but not more than that.
examples: We had adequate food for the trip, but nothing extra.
The small tent was adequate for two people.
Her answer was adequate, but she could have given more detail.

easy.def: To stick to something.
examples: Glue will adhere.
The tape adhered to the paper.
The sticker adheres well.

more.def: To stick firmly to something, or to follow a rule.
examples: The sticker adheres to the wall.
We must adhere to the rules of the game.
Wet snow adheres to your boots.

easy.def: Glue or tape that sticks things together.
examples: Glue is an adhesive.
The adhesive is sticky.
Tape is an adhesive.

more.def: A substance such as glue or tape that sticks things together.
examples: A strong adhesive held the broken cup together.
The adhesive on the stamp is on the back.
An adhesive held the picture to the wall.

easy.def: Sticky.
examples: Adhesive tape sticks.
The adhesive label stuck.
I saw an adhesive bandage.

more.def: Able to stick to things.
examples: Adhesive tape holds the paper down.
The adhesive label stuck to the box.
She covered the cut with an adhesive bandage.

easy.def: A word that tells more about a noun.
examples: "Big" is an adjective.
An adjective describes a thing.
Find the adjective.

more.def: A word that describes a noun, such as "red," "big" or "happy."
examples: "Happy" is an adjective in the sentence "She is happy."
An adjective tells what kind or how many.
Circle each adjective in the sentence.

easy.def: Next to each other and joined.
examples: We had adjoining rooms.
The adjoining door opened.
An adjoining yard.

more.def: Next to something and joined to it.
examples: We stayed in adjoining rooms at the hotel.
The adjoining door led to the kitchen.
Our house and the adjoining field belong to Grandpa.

easy.def: To change a little to make it better.
examples: I adjust my seat.
She adjusted her hat.
He adjusted the volume.

more.def: To change something slightly so that it fits or works better.
examples: I adjusted my seat in the car.
She adjusted the straps on her backpack.
He adjusted the volume on the radio.

easy.def: A small change to make something better.
examples: I made an adjustment to my chair.
Dad made an adjustment to the seat.
A small adjustment fixed it.

more.def: A small change made so that something works better or fits well.
examples: Dad made a small adjustment to the bike seat.
It took some adjustment to get used to the new school.
The coach made an adjustment to the team's plan at halftime.

easy.def: To give something to someone, such as medicine.
examples: The nurse administered the medicine.
The teacher administers the test.
She administered first aid.

more.def: To give or provide something, or to manage something.
examples: The nurse administered the medicine to the patient.
The teacher administered the test to the whole class.
A principal helps administer the school.

easy.def: The people who run a school or a group.
examples: The administration made a plan.
Ask the school administration.
The administration is in the office.

more.def: The people or work of running an organization such as a school.
examples: The school administration sent a letter to parents.
The administration decided to build a new gym.
She works in the administration of the hospital.

easy.def: A person who helps run a school or company.
examples: The administrator spoke.
She is an administrator.
The administrator helped.

more.def: A person whose job is to manage or run an organization such as a school or hospital.
examples: The school administrator greeted the new parents.
An administrator helped plan the trip.
Hospital administrators plan how to use the money.

easy.def: A very high officer in the navy.
examples: The admiral was on the ship.
The admiral gave an order.
The admiral wore a uniform.

more.def: The most important officer in a navy, who leads many ships.
examples: The admiral led the fleet of ships.
The admiral wore a uniform with gold stripes.
The sailors saluted the admiral.

easy.def: A strong liking and respect for someone.
examples: She looked with admiration.
I have admiration for my teacher.
He showed admiration.

more.def: A feeling of respect and liking for someone or something that you think is very good.
examples: She looked at her older sister with admiration.
I have great admiration for firefighters.
The crowd clapped in admiration.

easy.def: To think someone or something is very good.
examples: I admire my big sister.
We admire the pretty rainbow.
I admire how fast you can run.

more.def: To respect and look up to someone, or to enjoy looking at something.
examples: We stopped to admire the colorful sunset.
The students admire their coach for never giving up.
Visitors admired the tall towers of the old castle.

easy.def: A person who likes and respects someone.
examples: She has many admirers.
He is an admirer of the artist.
I am an admirer of my teacher.

more.def: A person who thinks very well of someone or something.
examples: The singer has many admirers who love her songs.
He is a big admirer of the artist's work.
I am an admirer of my teacher, who is kind and wise.

easy.def: In a way that shows you like something a lot.
examples: She looked admiringly at the painting.
He smiled admiringly.
They watched admiringly.

more.def: In a way that shows you think someone or something is very good.
examples: The children looked admiringly at the tall trophy.
She gazed admiringly at the artist's work.
He watched admiringly as the skater spun on the ice.

easy.def: The cost to go in.
examples: Admission is five dollars.
The admission was free.
We paid admission.

more.def: The price you pay to get into a place, or the act of letting someone in.
examples: Admission to the museum is five dollars.
The park gave free admission on Sunday.
The school's admission process takes weeks.

easy.def: To say that something is true.
examples: I admit I ate the cookie.
He admitted he was late.
She admits she is wrong.

more.def: To agree that something is true, especially something you did not want to say.
examples: I admit that I ate the last cookie.
He admitted that he was scared.
She admitted she had forgotten her lunch.

easy.def: Permission to go in.
examples: No admittance.
Admittance is free.
The sign said no admittance.

more.def: Permission or the right to go in.
examples: The sign said "No admittance."
Admittance to the museum is free for children.
Only members were given admittance.

easy.def: As you must say is true.
examples: It is admittedly small.
Admittedly, I was late.
He was admittedly wrong.

more.def: Used when you agree that something is true, even if it is not good.
examples: The hill was admittedly steep, but the view was great.
Admittedly, I forgot my hat.
The test was admittedly hard, but I did my best.

easy.def: A building brick made of dried mud and straw.
examples: The house is adobe.
Adobe is made of mud.
An adobe wall.

more.def: A building material made of clay and straw dried in the sun, or a house made of it.
examples: The house was built of adobe.
Adobe keeps a house cool in the hot sun.
An adobe wall surrounded the courtyard.

easy.def: The years when you change from a child to an adult.
examples: Adolescence is the teen years.
He is in adolescence.
Adolescence is a time of change.

more.def: The time of life between being a child and being an adult.
examples: Adolescence is when kids grow quickly.
In adolescence, a person's voice may change.
The book is about growing up in adolescence.

easy.def: To take a child or pet into your family as your own.
examples: We adopted a puppy.
They adopted a baby.
I want to adopt a cat.

more.def: To take a child or an animal into your family and care for it as your own.
examples: Our family adopted a kitten from the shelter.
They adopted a baby girl last year.
She wants to adopt a dog.

easy.def: To start using a new idea or way of doing something.
examples: The class adopted a new rule.
We adopted a new plan.
The school adopted a new book.

more.def: To choose and begin to use something such as a plan or a rule.
examples: The town adopted a rule about recycling.
Our club adopted a new name.
The school adopted a new reading program.

easy.def: Taking a child or pet to be part of your family.
examples: We went to a pet adoption day.
Their adoption made them a family.
The dog's adoption was on Saturday.

more.def: The act of taking someone or something into your family or care as your own.
examples: The family celebrated the adoption of their new baby sister.
We found our cat at an animal shelter adoption event.
The class voted for the adoption of a new rule.

easy.def: Having chosen a child to join the family.
examples: Her adoptive parents love her.
An adoptive family.
His adoptive mom.

more.def: Having taken a child into a family through adoption.
examples: Her adoptive parents love her very much.
They are an adoptive family with three children.
His adoptive mother read to him each night.

easy.def: So cute that you love it.
examples: The puppy is adorable.
The baby is adorable.
The kittens are adorable.

more.def: Very cute and lovable.
examples: The puppy was adorable in its little sweater.
The baby giggled in an adorable way.
The kittens looked adorable curled up together.

easy.def: To love very much.
examples: I adore my puppy.
She adores her grandma.
He adores ice cream.

more.def: To love someone or something very, very much.
examples: I adore my little sister.
She adores her pet rabbit.
The children adore the story about the dragon.

easy.def: Showing great love.
examples: The adoring fans cheered.
An adoring puppy.
She gave an adoring smile.

more.def: Showing great love and admiration.
examples: The adoring fans cheered the singer.
An adoring puppy followed her everywhere.
She gave her grandmother an adoring smile.

easy.def: To decorate something to make it look nice.
examples: Bows adorn the door.
She adorned the tree.
Lights adorned the house.

more.def: To decorate something so that it looks nicer.
examples: Flowers adorn the table.
She adorned the tree with shiny balls.
Lights adorned the house for the holiday.

easy.def: A chemical in the body that gives you a burst of energy.
examples: Adrenaline made me fast.
Adrenaline gives energy.
I felt adrenaline.

more.def: A chemical made by the body when you are excited or scared, which makes your heart beat faster and gives you a burst of energy.
examples: Adrenaline made my heart pound as I stood at the top of the slide.
The runner felt a rush of adrenaline at the start of the race.
Adrenaline helps your body get ready to act quickly.

easy.def: A person who is not a child.
examples: An adult drove us.
Ask an adult for help.
Adults go to work.

more.def: A person or animal that has finished growing.
examples: Kids must go with an adult on the trip.
An adult elephant weighs thousands of pounds.
She is an adult now and lives in her own apartment.

easy.def: The time when you are a grown-up.
examples: He reached adulthood.
Adulthood comes after childhood.
Adulthood is a time of work.

more.def: The time of life when a person is fully grown.
examples: Adulthood begins after childhood and the teen years.
He reached adulthood at eighteen.
The book follows a boy from childhood to adulthood.

easy.def: To move forward.
examples: The line advanced.
The army advanced.
I advanced to the next level.

more.def: To move forward, or to make progress.
examples: The line of people slowly advanced.
She advanced to the next level of the game.
Science advances as we learn new things.

easy.def: A step forward.
examples: We made an advance in math.
An advance in science helps people.
Advances in medicine help us.

more.def: A move forward or an improvement in something.
examples: The scientists made an advance in medicine.
Advances in computers have changed our lives.
The advance of the army was slow.

easy.def: Far along, or more difficult.
examples: She is in the advanced class.
The advanced book is hard.
He has advanced skills.

more.def: Beyond the beginning, more difficult or more modern.
examples: She is in the advanced reading group.
The advanced class studies harder math.
The advanced machine can do many jobs.

easy.def: Moving forward or getting better.
examples: Computers show great advancement.
The advancement of medicine helps us.
There was advancement in the class.

more.def: The act of moving ahead, or a step forward in a job, an idea or a skill.
examples: Advancement in science has made life easier.
The new machine was a major advancement in farming.
She earned an advancement to the next level.

easy.def: Something that helps you do better.
examples: Being tall is an advantage in basketball.
Our team had the advantage.
Having a map is an advantage.

more.def: Something that puts you in a better position than others.
examples: Wearing boots was an advantage on the muddy trail.
A map gave the hikers an advantage over those without one.
The team had the advantage of playing on its own field.

easy.def: The arrival of something new.
examples: The advent of spring.
The advent of the car.
The advent of rain.

more.def: The coming or arrival of an important person, thing or time.
examples: We watched for the advent of spring.
The advent of the car changed how people traveled.
The advent of the new bridge helped the town.

easy.def: A fun and exciting trip or time.
examples: We went on an adventure in the woods.
My book is about an adventure at sea.
Camping in the yard was an adventure.

more.def: An exciting experience, often one that is new or a little bit risky.
examples: Sailing across the lake was the biggest adventure of her summer.
Their first plane ride felt like a great adventure.
The story follows a mouse on an adventure through the city.

easy.def: A person who likes to go to new, exciting places.
examples: The adventurer climbed a mountain.
An adventurer sailed far.
She is an adventurer.

more.def: A person who looks for exciting and new experiences.
examples: The adventurer sailed around the world.
An adventurer explored the cave.
The young adventurer hiked up the mountain.

easy.def: Liking to try new and exciting things.
examples: She is adventurous.
An adventurous boy climbed a tree.
The adventurous pup explored.

more.def: Willing to try new, exciting or risky things.
examples: The adventurous girl tried every ride at the fair.
An adventurous explorer crossed the jungle.
He is an adventurous eater who tries new foods.

easy.def: A person you are against in a game or fight.
examples: He beat his adversary.
The adversary was strong.
My adversary was clever.

more.def: An opponent; a person or team you compete against.
examples: He faced a clever adversary in the chess match.
The knight faced his adversary on the field.
The two teams were old adversaries.

easy.def: Bad or harmful.
examples: The weather was adverse.
An adverse effect.
The adverse conditions stopped us.

more.def: Harmful or not favorable.
examples: The adverse weather forced us to cancel the trip.
The medicine had an adverse effect.
The team played well in adverse conditions.

easy.def: To tell people about something so that they will buy it or come.
examples: The store advertises on the radio.
They advertised the show.
We advertise our sale with a sign.

more.def: To tell people about a product, a service or an event, so they will want to buy it or come to it.
examples: The bakery put up a sign to advertise its fresh bread.
The school advertised the book fair with colorful posters.
Many stores advertise their sales on television.

easy.def: A short message that tries to get you to buy something.
examples: I saw an advertisement on TV.
The advertisement had a song.
An advertisement for toys.

more.def: A picture, a message or a short video that tells people about something for sale and tries to get them to buy it.
examples: I saw an advertisement for a new toy on television.
The advertisement had a catchy song.
The newspaper had an advertisement for the circus.

easy.def: A person or company that makes ads.
examples: The advertiser made an ad.
An advertiser paid for it.
The advertiser sells shoes.

more.def: A person or company that tells people about a product to sell it.
examples: An advertiser paid for the commercial.
The advertiser made a colorful poster.
The advertiser tells people about the shoes.

easy.def: Telling people about things to buy.
examples: Advertising is on TV.
The store uses advertising.
Advertising helps sell things.

more.def: The business of making notices that try to get people to buy things.
examples: Advertising on TV tries to sell us toys.
The store spent money on advertising.
Her job is in advertising.

easy.def: Words that help someone decide what to do.
examples: I need your advice.
Her advice helped me.
Take my advice.

more.def: Words or ideas that help someone decide what to do.
examples: The coach gave me good advice.
I asked my teacher for advice.
Grandpa's advice helped me solve the problem.

easy.def: A good idea to do.
examples: It is advisable to wear a coat.
An advisable plan.
It is advisable to be early.

more.def: Wise and sensible to do.
examples: It is advisable to wear a coat in the snow.
It is advisable to check the weather first.
A map is advisable on the long hike.

easy.def: To tell someone what you think they should do.
examples: Mom advised me to wear a coat.
The doctor advises rest.
I advise you to take a map.

more.def: To give someone your opinion about what they should do.
examples: The coach advised us to drink water.
My teacher advised me to read every night.
The guide advised the hikers to stay on the path.

easy.def: A person who gives advice.
examples: The adviser helped us pick.
Our class has an adviser.
The adviser gave us tips.

more.def: A person whose job is to give advice and help people decide what to do.
examples: The student council has a teacher as its adviser.
The king listened to his wise adviser.
An adviser helped the club plan the trip.

easy.def: A person who speaks up for an idea or a group.
examples: She is an advocate for animals.
He is an advocate for parks.
The advocate spoke.

more.def: A person who speaks up in support of an idea, a cause or other people.
examples: She is an advocate for clean water.
The advocate asked the council to build a new playground.
He became an advocate for children who need books.
